context:
Split the work into two small centers of gravity: one query-resolution helper
and one execution-mode predicate. Route production mixin, dry-run, CLI, and
deprecated compatibility helpers through those centers. Keep compatibility
wrappers until deletion is separately authorized.
description:
Independent verification confirmed that DataFrame execution has two related
sources of drift.

The deprecated internal compatibility module
`benchbox/core/runner/dataframe_runner.py` is still load-bearing for CLI and
dry-run helpers. Production DataFrame execution uses
`adapter.run_benchmark()` through
`benchbox/platforms/dataframe/benchmark_mixin.py`, but dry-run imports
`get_execution_mode()` and `_get_queries_for_benchmark()` from the deprecated
module. Both the deprecated runner and the production mixin duplicate TPC-H
stream ordering, TPC-DS stream/variant fallback, and bidirectional query
subset filters.

DataFrame-vs-SQL routing is also detected two ways. The lifecycle runner
decides DataFrame execution from adapter `family in ("expression", "pandas")`,
while adapter factory, capabilities, CLI/dry-run helpers, and the deprecated
runner use platform suffix/default-mode logic. A new DataFrame family or
registry default can therefore disagree with the lifecycle branch.

anti_patterns.dont: decide DataFrame mode in runner.py by hard-coding family names again
anti_patterns.why: future families must not require runner edits.

anti_patterns.dont: delete `dataframe_runner.py` just because it is deprecated
anti_patterns.why: dry-run and tests still import it.

anti_patterns.dont: import optional DataFrame libraries in mode-detection helpers.
let dry-run call a different TPC-DS variant fallback implementation than real execution.
replace bidirectional Q-prefix filters with canonical stripping unless tests prove all caller contracts still work.

work_units.notes:
Extract the exact bidirectional query filter behavior currently duplicated
in `BenchmarkExecutionMixin._build_query_filter()` and
`dataframe_runner._execute_dataframe_queries()`:
  - input `Q1` matches both `Q1` and `1`;
  - input `1` matches both `1` and `Q1`;
  - case-insensitive input;
  - variant IDs such as `Q14a` remain usable.

Do not accidentally replace this with the existing one-way
`normalize_query_id()` helper unless the helper is extended to preserve
the bidirectional filter-set contract.

Reconcile, but do not necessarily replace, SQL adapter
`_apply_query_subset()`: it resolves against actual query dict keys and
is related rather than identical.
work_units.summary: Replace duplicated bidirectional Q-prefix filter normalization with one helper

work_units.notes:
Update `benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py` and `benchbox/core/dryrun.py` to use
the shared execution-mode and query-resolution helpers rather than
importing from `benchbox.core.runner.dataframe_runner`.

Leave `dataframe_runner.py` as a deprecated internal compatibility module
if tests or public-contract docs require it. Its helper functions should
delegate to the new shared helpers so behavior cannot drift.

Update docs/reference/backward-compatibility.md only if the lifecycle
status or removal timing changes.

    inputs.
